note.text: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms interacting with its non-living environment. A population consists of one species in an area; a community includes populations of different species. A habitat is where an organism lives, while its niche concerns its role and use of resources. Light, water, temperature and soil influence organisms; organisms can also modify these conditions. An ecosystem can be a pond, woodland or a larger landscape, so a boundary is chosen to suit the question.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify interacting living and non-living components and locate a model habitat on a grid. Builds on: soil as an open system and conservation. Leads to: energy transfer and nutrient cycling.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: An ecosystem includes a community of organisms interacting with its non-living environment. A population consists of one species in an area; a community includes populations of different species. A habitat is where an organism lives, while its niche concerns its role and use of resources. Light, water, temperature and soil influence organisms; organisms can also modify these conditions. An ecosystem can be a pond, woodland or a larger landscape, so a boundary is chosen to suit the question.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In a fictional school pond near Yaoundé, algae, insects and microbes interact with light, water and mineral nutrients. Water is an abiotic component even when it contains living organisms. The grid exercise locates a model pond using eastings before northings; it is not a real pond survey. A site label locates a place but does not measure its biodiversity or water quality.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Separate population, community and ecosystem by what each includes. Describe one interaction rather than only naming organisms. Check the map’s labelled lines before recording a grid square. Use classroom records rather than entering ponds or collecting unknown organisms.
